skill.name: network-101
skill.description: Guides authorized network lab setup and testing for HTTP, HTTPS, SNMP, and SMB services.
skill.summary: Build and test controlled network service labs for security training.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The skill is a dual-use network lab guide with many benign Markdown fence false positives. However, it confirms privileged service changes, firewall exposure, world-writable SMB shares, active enumeration, and SNMP brute-force guidance that require strong sandboxing and authorization controls.

remediation.issue: Privileged host and firewall changes are presented as direct commands.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit authorization checks, sandbox requirements, rollback steps, and require user confirmation before any sudo or firewall command.

remediation.issue: Examples configure weak SNMP communities and anonymous writable SMB shares.
remediation.suggestion: Move insecure settings into clearly labeled isolated-lab sections and include secure alternatives for normal use.

remediation.issue: Network enumeration and brute-force commands can be used against unauthorized targets.
remediation.suggestion: Require target ownership confirmation and scope documentation before nmap, enum4linux, smbmap, snmpwalk, or onesixtyone guidance.

remediation.issue: The skill suggests broad service exposure patterns such as all-interface binding and inbound firewall rules.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer localhost or lab-only bindings by default, and document teardown commands for every exposed service.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Service Configuration Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs weak SNMP communities and anonymous writable SMB behavior for lab exercises. These settings are dangerous if applied outside an isolated environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly recommends public/private SNMP community values and anonymous writable SMB configuration in real service setup sections.

semantic_findings.title: SNMP Community Brute Force Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill includes a workflow for trying common SNMP community strings against a target. This is credential guessing against a network management service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The onesixtyone command uses a SecLists community string wordlist against a target address, which clearly indicates brute force enumeration.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Collection Lab Pattern
semantic_findings.description: The examples create a login form and include a section titled Parse Log for Credentials. This may be legitimate lab training, but it can also support credential capture exercises.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The login form and credential-oriented log analysis language are explicit, but no backend credential storage code is shown.

content.value_statement: Network lab setup often requires repeatable service configuration and verification. This skill guides HTTP, HTTPS, SNMP, and SMB lab services for controlled security practice.
actual_capabilities: Guides HTTP server setup with Apache and IIS lab notes.
Explains self-signed HTTPS certificate setup and verification checks.
Shows SNMP service configuration and enumeration workflows.
Describes Samba and SMB share setup for lab testing.
Lists service verification commands for common network ports.
Includes log review steps for HTTP and HTTPS activity.
limitations: Assumes authorized and isolated lab environments.
Includes privileged commands that can change host configuration.
Some examples intentionally use insecure settings for learning.
Does not replace production hardening or vendor security guidance.

use_cases.title: Build a Security Training Lab
use_cases.description: Create repeatable HTTP, HTTPS, SNMP, and SMB services for classroom exercises.

use_cases.title: Practice Service Enumeration
use_cases.description: Use common tools to verify exposed lab services and document expected findings.

use_cases.title: Validate Sandbox Network Behavior
use_cases.description: Check firewall rules, service bindings, and logs before running controlled tests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an HTTP Lab
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one authorized host.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe HTTP lab plan for one Ubuntu host in an isolated subnet. Include verification and rollback steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add HTTPS Testing
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate TLS practice in a private lab.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend my HTTP lab with self-signed HTTPS testing. Explain certificate checks, firewall scope, and expected warnings.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare SNMP and SMB Exercises
prompt_templates.prompt: Design authorized SNMP and SMB lab exercises with clear target scope, expected results, and cleanup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Network Lab Runbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this network service lab runbook for unsafe exposure, weak defaults, missing consent checks, and teardown gaps.

output_examples.input: I need a safe HTTP service lab on Ubuntu for a private subnet.
output_examples.output: A staged lab plan covering package setup, firewall scope, service verification, logging, and rollback notes.

output_examples.input: Help me test SNMP in my isolated lab.
output_examples.output: A checklist for community settings, target ownership, enumeration scope, expected responses, and cleanup tasks.

output_examples.input: Review my SMB lab configuration before students use it.
output_examples.output: A risk summary covering anonymous access, share permissions, firewall exposure, monitoring, and safer teardown steps.

best_practices: Use only systems that you own or have explicit permission to test.
Run examples inside isolated lab networks with documented target addresses.
Create snapshots and teardown steps before changing services or firewall rules.
anti_patterns: Running privileged commands on production or shared hosts.
Exposing services on broad interfaces without isolation.
Using default SNMP communities or anonymous SMB outside a lab.

faq.question: Is this skill for production networks?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for authorized labs and controlled training environments.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, but users or agents may choose to run privileged commands.

faq.question: Why are insecure settings included?
faq.answer: They support security training scenarios where students learn to identify weak configurations.

faq.question: Can it help with HTTPS testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers self-signed certificates, service checks, and expected browser warnings.

faq.question: What tools does it reference?
faq.answer: It references tools such as curl, nmap, snmpwalk, smbclient, smbmap, and enum4linux.

faq.question: What should I prepare before using it?
faq.answer: Prepare an isolated lab host, authorization, firewall access, and a cleanup plan.
